status: Production source frozen; no native performance or visual claim from these tests
problem: Light CPU trace identified roughly35ms body-generation work in several80ms callbacks; this change moves eligible cached replacement generation to a client-owned worker. It does not attribute/remove the full172ms task whose largest sampled owner was GC.

scope.firstSight: Existing synchronous priority/build-budget/proxy path preserved; only already-published cached replacement can be asynchronous.
scope.ownership: Pure imports do not registerFleet or create Worker. Dedicated worker entry registers once; explicit main service creation occurs after normal fleet registration. Only a fresh result Float32 buffer is transferred; retained worker rest/binding and main geometry are never transferred.
scope.publication: Current key observed on every eligible cached draw before targeted publication immediately before that body emits. One shared ordinary publication lane alternates ready results against bounded FIFO of waiting first-sight/sync fallback bodies; no second view/motion sample. All main/shadow/planar geometry uses that emitted source. Existing cubemap complete-sweep temporal policy remains.

correctness.progress: Valid completed active work may publish while newer desired input waits; exact desired ready work is preserved against a different completion. Returning A→B→A or B→C→B cancels obsolete pending/ready work. Every sync publication advances incarnation and fences late worker replies.
correctness.cleanup: Offscreen/incompatible residents release active/pending/ready ownership at frame boundary without deleting main cached geometry; active reservation remains until reply/timeout. Freeing ready budget immediately wakes other visible pending work. Same-ID live type replacement removes incompatible main/controller body/rest ownership first.
correctness.failure: Unavailable/failed/mismatched/malformed/timed-out worker returns to exact caller-owned sync path. Error/watchdog callback never executes a generator. Source/config/staged/page lifecycle fences outstanding results.

frozenSyncOracle.coverage: Full active output Float64 body stream and Float32 primitive geometry/matrix bytes for absent/unavailable service, priority/first sight/motion/doors. Focused live flow checks pending geometry identity, current pose/wheels, targeted output, cyclic keys, source/staged/type boundaries, sustained ready cap-denied taxi/unsupported bike fairness, hidden residency and180-ID FIFO.

browser.comparison: Every Float32 output bit via Uint32 arrays against frozen current body branch; includes all five families × three wireframe modes, distinct resolved spec, large sculpt/damaged/open body, rest/current deformation transitions, style boundary and signed zero/ordinary-array inputs.
browser.cleanup: Browser,CDP,dedicated temporary profile and local server closed. CPU-only headless Chrome with GPU disabled; no rendered-frame/native capture.

limitations: No FPS/long-task/GC improvement claimed before root-owned fixed-quality native capture and actual activity/geometry guard.
Synchronous first sight, priority and worker failure paths can still tessellate on main; compile/pack/GPU publication remains main-thread work.

Immediate legacy priority rebuild may exceed the ordinary lane and can delay ordinary work during continuously changing priority frames. This existing exception is not advertised as an absolute one-publication/frame or unconditional fairness guarantee.
Payload/rest/spec/binding accounting does not equal JS heap usage; procedural temporary number arrays and module caches still allocate. Output cap is checked after exact generation.
Worker parameter-cache lifetime budget fails closed to sync after64variants/1MiB key text; automatic worker rotation is not implemented.
The180-ID deferred FIFO covers the existing live admission budget, which is unchanged; no absolute fairness promise for out-of-contract fixtures exceeding that cap.
Browser buildMs fields are individual diagnostic job durations, not warmed timing/FPS results.
